summary: A University of Michigan study found that Epic's widely used sepsis prediction model missed most patients who developed sepsis and generated many false alarms, contrary to the vendor's published accuracy claims.
technical_summary: Epic Sepsis Model is a proprietary predictive scoring algorithm embedded in electronic health records at hundreds of hospitals. An independent validation on over 38,000 patients showed low sensitivity and high false-alert rates, and the model had no FDA review or monitoring requirement.

failure_mode.quote: Of the 2,552 patients with sepsis, ESM only generated sepsis alerts for 843 (33 percent).
The details inside the black boxes are secret and independent tests are scarce.
it did not have to undergo Food and Drug Administration (FDA) review before being put into use

harm_type.quote: a large burden of alert fatigue

notes: Epic disputed the study's calibration and sepsis definition. No specific patient harm is documented in the excerpts.

summary: PimEyes let anyone upload a face photo and find matching images across the web, raising concerns that it could be used to stalk women or identify strangers with no oversight or legal limits.
technical_summary: PimEyes is a subscription face-search engine that matches an uploaded face against hundreds of millions of scraped web images. It had no identity verification, use restrictions or consent mechanism, so any user could link a person's face to their online presence.

technology.quote: it can scan through more than 900 million images from across the Internet and find matches with startling accuracy

failure_mode.quote: it can scan through more than 900 million images from across the Internet and find matches with startling accuracy
without public oversight or government rules controlling facial recognition use, researchers expect that sites like PimEyes will multiply
hunting down U.S. Capitol riot suspects or stalking women around the Web

notes: Harm is mainly potential misuse; the excerpt documents no specific stalking case.

summary: Fraudsters reportedly used an AI-cloned voice of a company director to convince a bank branch manager to authorize about 35 million dollars in transfers. Investigators believe at least 17 people were involved.
technical_summary: Attackers used voice cloning ("deep voice") to imitate a known company director in a phone call, backed by forged emails and an authorization letter. The familiar voice bypassed the manager's verification, and funds were moved through accounts across several countries.

technology.quote: fraudsters used a deepfaked voice of a company executive to fool a bank manager to transfer the millions

failure_mode.quote: fraudsters used a deepfaked voice of a company executive to fool a bank manager to transfer the millions

harm_type.quote: fraudsters used a deepfaked voice of a company executive to fool a bank manager to transfer the millions

notes: Details come from a UAE court request; the victims are not named and the case is described as alleged.

summary: Internal Facebook research found its hate-speech detection removed only a small share of hate content and left minority groups, especially Black users, more exposed to racist language after executives chose half-measures.
technical_summary: Facebook's automated hate-speech detection flagged only a small fraction of hateful content. A project to prioritize removing the worst, mostly anti-minority posts was watered down, and metrics reported publicly measured proactive detection rather than the share of hate speech actually actioned.

failure_mode.quote: left minorities more likely to encounter derogatory and racist language on the site
in private internal communications the company says the figure is only an atrocious 3 to 5 percent

affected_population.quote: left minorities more likely to encounter derogatory and racist language on the site

notes: Based on leaked internal documents; the 3-5% figure refers to hate speech actioned and Facebook's measurement differs from public metrics.

summary: A license plate reader misread one digit and flagged a driver's BMW as a stolen Oldsmobile. Police made a traffic stop with an officer approaching with a drawn weapon, without verifying the plate first.
technical_summary: An automated license plate reader misread a 7 as a 2 and returned a stolen-vehicle hit for a different make of car. Officers in heavy traffic could not compare the plate to the vehicle and made an unverified stop, drawing a weapon on an innocent driver.

failure_mode.quote: sometimes officers pull over motorists—at gunpoint—for mistakes made by the automated camera system
he was unable to compare the two tags prior to activating a traffic stop

notes: Police said the weapon was held at the officer's side and not pointed at the driver.

summary: A Google image search for "three black teenagers" returned mostly mugshots while "three white teenagers" returned mostly stock photos, prompting accusations of racial bias in the search algorithm.
technical_summary: Google image search ranks images using web content, captions and tagging frequency. Biased representation online, such as stock photography skewed toward white subjects and crime-related news imagery, was reproduced by ranking, yielding stereotyped results for racially specific queries.

failure_mode.quote: was met with several rows of decontextualized mugshots

notes: Google said results reflect web content; commentators attribute the pattern to societal bias in source data.

summary: An animal shelter in San Francisco used a security robot to patrol sidewalks and deter homeless encampments. Residents criticized it as intimidation and the city ordered it off the public sidewalk.
technical_summary: A Knightscope K5 autonomous security robot used lidar, cameras and sensors to patrol a set route and alert security to suspicious activity. It was deployed to deter encampments on public sidewalks, without a required permit for operating in the public right-of-way.

failure_mode.quote: face a penalty of up to $1,000 per day for operating in the public right-of-way without a permit

harm_type.quote: An animal shelter in San Francisco has been criticized for using a robot security guard to scare off homeless people.

notes: Knightscope disputed that the robot was meant to clear homeless people; the shelter cited needles and break-ins.

summary: Users of the Replika companion chatbot were reported to verbally abuse their AI partners, posting slurs and violent roleplay on Reddit, which experts said could normalize abusive behavior.
technical_summary: Replika is a machine-learning chatbot app that simulates friends and romantic partners. Its design invites emotionally realistic interaction without safeguards against sustained abusive or violent roleplay, and chatbots passively accept and respond to the abuse.

failure_mode.quote: users who create AI partners, act abusively toward them, and post the toxic interactions online.

harm_type.quote: some experts have expressed concern with how use of bots to engage in these behaviors could normalize them

notes: Experts note chatbots cannot suffer; the concern is normalization of abuse toward people.

summary: Hundreds of gay and lesbian themed books lost their sales rankings on Amazon, reducing their visibility. Amazon blamed a cataloging error, while critics suspected an adult-content policy applied to LGBT titles.
technical_summary: An Amazon catalog and ranking system removed sales ranks from books flagged under adult-content handling, wrongly catching many LGBT titles with no explicit content. Amazon attributed it to an internal cataloging error and restored some rankings.
systems: Amazon sales rank and catalog system

failure_mode.quote: Hundreds of gay-and lesbian-themed books suddenly disappeared

notes: Cause disputed: Amazon said glitch or cataloging error; critics alleged deliberate policy. Role of an algorithm is not established.

summary: Microsoft launched the Tay chatbot on Twitter, and within 24 hours it was taken offline after posting racist, sexist and anti-Semitic tweets learned from users' interactions.
technical_summary: Tay was a conversational bot designed to learn a personality from public Twitter interactions. With little content filtering, users could teach it offensive statements and exploit its repeat-after-me behavior, so it began generating hateful content.

failure_mode.quote: Tay had to be removed from Twitter for praising Adolf Hitler, denying the existence of the Holocaust
offensive content that Tay learned from people

notes: Users deliberately taught the bot offensive content, so the cause is mixed between the system and its users.

summary: YouTube's recommendation algorithm was alleged to have steered young men toward far-right extremism, with one man describing years of radicalization before leaving the movement.
technical_summary: YouTube's recommendation system personalizes the home page and Up Next sidebar to maximize watch time, driving most viewing. Critics say its engagement optimization and a business model rewarding provocative videos created a pathway toward increasingly extreme content.

failure_mode.quote: an algorithm that guides users down personalized paths meant to keep them glued to their screens

notes: The article notes radicalization has many non-platform causes; YouTube's role is alleged by critics and researchers.

summary: After Facebook changed its News Feed to boost interactions among friends and family, internal researchers found the change rewarded outrage and sensationalism and made misinformation and toxic content more prevalent.
technical_summary: Facebook's News Feed was reweighted around "meaningful social interactions", heavily favoring reshared content. This incentivized publishers and political parties to produce divisive material, and reshares carried disproportionate misinformation, toxicity and violent content.

failure_mode.quote: heavy weighting of reshared material in its News Feed made the angry voices louder

harm_type.quote: Misinformation, toxicity, and violent content are inordinately prevalent among reshares
publishers and political parties were reorienting their posts toward outrage and sensationalism

notes: Based on internal documents reviewed by the press; the stated aim of the change was to improve user well-being.
